Fashion designs are partially protected under U.S. [d5] copyright law, but the protection is limited to specific elements — such as surface patterns, graphic designs, and logos — rather than the overall design of clothing or functional apparel items. [d5] Under the 1976 Copyright Act, useful articles like clothing are generally not protectable as copyrighted works unless they contain separable artistic elements that qualify as pictorial, graphic, or sculptural works on their own. [d5] Additionally, the Copyright Office has historically considered extending sui generis protection to fashion designs similar to that provided for vessel hull designs under Chapter 13 of Title 17, though no such broad legislation has been enacted for fashion specifically. [d5] In practice, fashion designers often rely on a combination of intellectual property tools — including copyright for surface elements, trademark law for logos and brand identity, and sometimes design rights or patents — to protect their creations. [d5]
[[END-OF-ANSWER]]
